correctness.rationale: q_t=x[1+t(1−x)] and 1−q_t=(1−x)(1−tx) imply the exact logit derivative 1+t²x(1−x)/{[1+t(1−x)](1−tx)}; all factors positive in the open interval for t in [−1,1]. A nontrivial word gives strictly increasing logit displacement, whose endpoint limits are log prod(1+t_j) and −log prod(1−t_j), including vanishing factors. Thus exactly one interior fixed point iff both endpoint products <1; its original multiplier is >1 by cancellation of coordinate derivatives. Near a regular piecewise orbit the map agrees with its word, establishing that corollary. The standalone SymPy checker verified the exact identity and rational 2-cycle with return multiplier 27389/22440; 776 finite rational word cases check consistency only.

value.rationale: Arbitrary exogenous switching and spatially state-dependent quadratic heredity maps are natural dynamical models. Previous derivative>1 proof only handles a special one-cut sign-ordered region; outside that region individual Euclidean derivatives can be less than one, so repulsion is not a routine parameter continuation. The exact product test classifies existence uniquely for every finite word and globally excludes regular attracting cycles across any finite partition. This provides structural stability constraints and a precise admissibility algorithm for periodic population configurations.
